key_insight: Menopause timing showed a nonlinear association with blood NfL and a linear association with GDF-15, but no significant associations with GFAP or p-tau181.
clinical_relevance: These findings may inform research into menopause-related dementia risk but do not establish causation or support individual risk prediction.
method: Observational analysis of the population-based U.S. Health and Retirement Study.
Related self-reported menopause timing to four blood biomarkers measured in 2016, adjusting for sociodemographic and health factors.
Evaluated APOE ε4 effect modification and hysterectomy history in additional analyses.
evidence_signal: Among 893 women without hysterectomy, menopause at later ages within 50–55 was associated with lower NfL (−0.031 SD/year; 95% CI, −0.051 to −0.011); later menopause was also associated with lower GDF-15 overall.
watch_item: The abstract is truncated, and this observational biomarker analysis does not demonstrate effects on dementia incidence.
paper_title: Age at Menopause and Dementia Risk: Blood-Based Biomarker Evidence from a US National Study
